data.title: Middle East Eye: ‘Spiritual darkness’: US ambassador to Israel says critics of Iran war are blinded by Satan
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
‘Spiritual darkness’: US ambassador to Israel says critics of Iran war are blinded by Satan
US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has drawn criticism after saying that critics of US war on Iran are "in spiritual darkness" and claiming that those who disagree with intervention have been blinded by Satan.
Huckabee's comments were posted online over the weekend, attracting backlash from conservative commentators who called for him to be removed from his role as a diplomat.
The comments were made during a live interview with Israeli commentator Amir Tsarfati on The Anchor Podcast.
In the interview published on October 23 by Behold Israel, Tsarfati asked Huckabee to comment on the attitude of European governments towards US military action against Iran. He asked if there was a "mental issue" or a "spiritual issue."
“I think it's a spiritual issue,” Huckabee replied.
“I know it sounds a little funny for an ambassador to be talking like this, but look, I see this as spiritual darkness, spiritual blindness.”
He continued: “Because Satan has blinded the minds of those and has captured their thinking.”
“I really do believe that there is something deeper than just the obvious geopolitical issues at bay,” he added.

data.title: Middle East Eye: What is happening in the occupied West Bank?
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
What is happening in the occupied West Bank?
Three Palestinians have been wounded after being severely beaten with clubs by Israeli settlers near Salfit city in the central occupied West Bank, Wafa reports, citing local sources.
According to the sources, the group were attacked in the Wadi al-Shaer area, and suffered severe wounds to their heads, abdomens and lower spines, with one of them sustaining a broken jaw.
Meanwhile, in the town of Sinjil, northeast of Ramallah, Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians farmers attempting to gather the olive harvest, seizing one of their vehicles.
In Jerusalem, the Israeli authroities issued demolition and stop-work notices for four residential and agricultural structures in the community of Abu al-Nuwar, near the town of al-Eizariya.
The Palestinian-run Jerusalem Governorate said this comes just days after the authorities announced the closure of the only read leading to Abu al-Nuwar, as well as the nearby al-Wadi al-A'raj and al-Muntar areas.
Meanwhile, Al Jazeera reports that Israel deported 14 western activists who were attempting to protect Palestinians as they harvested their olives. The Human Rights Defenders Fund said the group were arrested on Friday near Ramallah after being atacked by Israeli settlers.
October has seen an unprecedented surge in Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians attempting gather the olive harvest compared to previous years. OCHA documented 377 olive-harvest-related settler attacks across the West Bank between September 1 and November 2, 2026, outstripping the total recorded during a any previous olive harvest season.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran suggests blasts are not US attacks as both sides report ships hit
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Iran suggests blasts are not US attacks as both sides report ships hit
Iranian media suggested explosions in southern Iran on Saturday evening were related to Iranian military activities rather than US strikes while both sides reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's state television said officials had not confirmed any missile strikes on Iranian territory following blasts heard in several areas, including on Qeshm Island in the strait.
President Donald ​Trump had hinted at renewing major attacks on Iran ​after ⁠last week's US midterm elections but there has been no sign of a large-scale US military operation, which Iran has said it would respond to by striking US and Israeli targets.
Both sides have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, however, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy.
Iran's state television said the evening explosions might be related to Iranian military activity in the waterway, where Iran said two vessels had hit mines and a third had caught fire.
The US said its air force had disabled a vessel in the Gulf of Oman beyond the strait.
Tasnim news agency said two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, with no official information on possible damage. Neither Iran nor the US has commented on that report. Washington said on November 2 that it had struck the island in a limited defensive measure against Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets.
Reporting by Reuters

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'Iron Gate plan is merely wordplay': Iran mocks US military initiative to disrupt supply routes
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
'Iron Gate plan is merely wordplay': Iran mocks US military initiative to disrupt supply routes
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has dismissed a new US military initiative to restrict the movement of goods through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea as “merely wordplay”, as tensions over shipping routes and Washington's blockade continue.
“The Iron Gate plan is merely wordplay. The Americans cannot achieve their objectives of imposing severe economic pressure to cause economic collapse in Iran through this approach,” IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi told the semi-official Fars news agency on Sunday, according to Reuters.
Mohebbi said Washington had previously predicted that Iran would suffer economic collapse within two weeks, but that this had not happened.
Tehran had prepared for economic pressure and maintained close relations with neighbouring countries, he said.
The response came after US Central Command (Centcom) announced the establishment of Task Force Iron Gate on Saturday.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran's Araghchi calls on the US to end war 'on all fronts'
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Iran's Araghchi calls on the US to end war 'on all fronts'
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Aragchi called on the White House to "meet the requirements" of Tehran's 2-day proposal and "end to war on all fronts" on Sunday.
In a post on X, Aragchi wrote that "American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own," referring to the US President Donald Trump's defeats in the recent midterm elections.
He warned that if the Trump administration chooses war, it will will "see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell."
In a separate post, the Foreign Ministry quoted Araghchi on X, warning, “There are some American targets in the region outside military bases that may be within range of Iranian strikes.”
American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own. Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results. Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump says fresh strikes on Iran ‘highly unlikely’ if talks progress
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Trump says fresh strikes on Iran ‘highly unlikely’ if talks progress
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that renewed strikes on Iran are “highly unlikely” provided negotiations progress over Tehran's nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
“It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump said in a phone interview reported by CNN, adding: “I would, if necessary, but we hit them really hard.”
Trump said that three aircraft carriers are stationed in the region that are “fully locked and loaded” and there are 38 Iranian bridges that he said “we can knock down in literally one hour”.
Meanwhile, he said that the Iranian government maintains 10 percent of its missile capacity and 15 percent of its drone capabilities.

data.author: Fleur Hargreaves

Gaza sandbank collapse kills five amid heavy rains
At least five people have been killed, including three children, after heavy rains caused a sandbank to collapse in central Gaza's Deir al-Balah, Wafa news reported on Sunday.
A civil defence spokesman added that five wounded people had been pulled out of the rubble after their tents were hit, and teams are continuing to search for survivors.
The incident comes amid worsening conditions faced by displaced Palestinians in Gaza, as national and internation institutions warned heavy rainfall and bad weather require urgent intervention and the provision of safe shelter and winter supplies.

Iraq has agreed with the US to allow oil exports through Hormuz, minister says
Iraq has reached understandings with the US to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an interview with Al Jazeera.
He added that Iraq's losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 billion.
Hussein also told Al Jazeera that the US Treasury has asked Iraq to close all border crossings with Iran except for two as part of Washington's policy of increasing economic pressure on Tehran, with one of the exceptions being in the Kurdistan region.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that there has been no progress in mediators' work regarding peace talks between Tehran and Washington to end hostilities in the region since the results of the US midterm elections.
“The main reason is the US election results, which have obviously come as a shock to everyone,” Araghchi told reporters.
“It will take some time for things to settle down and for the atmosphere to become conducive to the mediators resuming their visits. We have to wait,” he added.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Eisenkot says any party involved in next government must commit to action on Hamas
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Eisenkot says any party involved in next government must commit to action on Hamas
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has said that any party willing to sign on to the “recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organisation and a commitment to destroying its military and governing capabilities” is a potential partner in his national emergency government.
Earlier, Israeli President Isaac Herzog officially gave Eisenkot six weeks to try to form the next government after the success of the anti-Netanyahu bloc in the recent Israeli elections.
“Israel does not have the luxury of wasting time or returning to endless rounds of elections. The challenges are too urgent,” he said in a speech alongside Herzog, adding that Israel is “in the midst of a destructive diplomatic crisis” as its closest allies are reconsidering their relations with the country.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog (R) and opposition bloc leader Gadi Eisenkot during a press conefernce at the President's office in Jerusalem on 8 November 2026 (Ilia Yefimovich/AFP)
